phrases.text: Question 1 would add a fundamental right to reproductive freedom.
Today, Virginia's Constitution provides no explicit right to reproductive freedom.
It would cover decisions about prenatal care, childbirth, postpartum care, birth control, abortion, miscarriage management and fertility care.
Doctors, nurses and patients could not be punished for those decisions.
The state could regulate third-trimester abortion care, but must allow it when medically needed to protect the life and health of the pregnant person, or when the fetus is not viable.
The Department of Planning and Budget estimates $205,000 for public notice of statewide referendums, not the amendment itself.
Virginia's explanation includes no official argument against the amendment.
Virginia's explanation includes no official argument for the amendment.
A yes vote adds the right to reproductive freedom.
A no vote leaves the Constitution unchanged.
